# Timestamp

Recognizes a copied Unix timestamp or date and tells you which moment it is. The item gets a small *time* chip; its preview shows the local time, UTC, ISO 8601, how long ago it was, the weekday and the Unix seconds. On a tagged item, ⇧ offers four conversions, each with its result as a hint.

## What it recognizes

The **whole copied text** must be one timestamp, between 1 January 1990 and 31 December 2099 (UTC):

- Unix seconds (10 digits), milliseconds (13), microseconds (16) and nanoseconds (19). With ten digits the range starts in September 2001, because 9-digit values cannot be told from other numbers.
- ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 date-times: `2026-01-01T03:00:00+03:00`, `2026-01-01T00:00:00.123Z`, `2026-01-01 00:00`, with `Z`, an offset (`+03:00`, `+0300`) or none. Fractions of a second up to nine digits are kept.
- RFC 2822 dates: `Thu, 1 Jan 2026 00:00:00 +0000`, with a numeric offset or `UT`, `GMT`, `EST`, `EDT`, `CST`, `CDT`, `MST`, `MDT`, `PST`, `PDT`. A weekday that does not match the date is refused.

A date or time without a zone is read in this Mac's time zone, and the preview says so ("Read as").

Not tagged: phone numbers and ids that only look like timestamps (wrong length, a leading zero, outside the range), years alone, dates without a time, invalid dates such as 30 February, leap seconds (`:60`) and `24:00`.

## Example

Copy `1767225600`. The preview shows `January 1, 2026 at 3:00:00 AM GMT+3` (local), the same moment in UTC, `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`, a relative time ("3 days ago" on the day this example was written), the weekday ("Thursday") and `1767225600`. In Turkish the same preview reads "1 Ocak 2026 03:00:00 GMT+3", "3 gün önce", "Perşembe".

## Actions

On a tagged item: *Convert to ISO 8601 (UTC)*, *Convert to Unix seconds*, *Convert to Unix milliseconds*, *Convert to local date and time*. Sub-millisecond digits survive in the ISO form (`2026-01-01T00:00:00.123456789Z`).

Anywhere: *Paste now as Unix seconds* and *Paste now as ISO 8601*.

## Setting

**Extra time zone** (empty by default): an IANA zone such as `America/New_York` or `Europe/London`. When set, the preview adds a row in that zone, with its abbreviation so daylight saving is clear. An invalid zone is ignored.

## Permissions

None. The extension only reads the item it is asked about and the clock. Nothing is sent anywhere, and no command-line tool is needed.

## Limits

- Dates are formatted by the system's `Intl`, so wording follows macOS.
- Text without a zone is read in this Mac's time. A time inside a spring-forward gap is shifted by the system, and an ambiguous fall-back time resolves to one of its two instants.
- Relative time is rounded ("3 months ago" is about 91 days).
- Millisecond precision is the finest a pasted Unix or ISO value keeps in the preview's local and UTC rows; the ISO row and the conversions keep nanoseconds.
readmes.dev.yabbistir.secret-guard:
# Secret Guard

Keeps the API keys, tokens, private keys and other secrets you copy out of your yabbistir history.

Password managers mark what they copy as concealed, and yabbistir never stores those copies. A key copied from a terminal, a `.env` file or a web dashboard arrives unmarked, and without Secret Guard it stays in your history for months. Secret Guard looks at each new copy before it is stored and, when the copy is or contains a secret, never writes it to your history.

That is all it does. It never changes your clipboard: the copy still pastes normally this time, as often as you like until you copy something else. It is simply never written to history, so it is not there to find, search or paste later. With the Stack open, such a copy does not join the Stack either.

## Example

Copy `export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_…` from a terminal and paste it into another one: it pastes as usual, and it is not in your history.

Copy a whole `.env` file:

```sh
NODE_ENV=production
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_…
SESSION_SECRET="…"
PORT=3000
```

It pastes into your new project as usual. Your history never gets the file, harmless lines included: a copy that holds a secret is left out whole.

## What it catches

Only formats it can recognize with high confidence: a known prefix, a fixed length or shape, or a label that names the value.

- **GitHub** tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`) and **GitLab** tokens (`glpat-`, and the deploy, runner, trigger and OAuth tokens).
- **AWS** access key ids (`AKIA…`, `ASIA…`), and secret access keys and session tokens where a label names them: `aws_secret_access_key = …` in a credentials file, `"SecretAccessKey": "…"` in the command line's output. A presigned S3 link carries a key id too, and is left out: anyone who has it can open the file until it expires.
- **Stripe** secret and restricted keys, live and test (`sk_live_`, `sk_test_`, `rk_live_`, `rk_test_`).
- **Slack** tokens (`xoxb-`, `xoxp-`, `xapp-` and the others) and webhook addresses (`hooks.slack.com/services/…`). The documentation's sample webhook, ending in `XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`, is kept.
- **Google** API keys (`AIza…`), **OpenAI** keys (`sk-proj-…`, `sk-svcacct-…`, `sk-admin-…` and the older `sk-` keys of 48 characters), **Anthropic** keys (`sk-ant-…`).
- **npm** (`npm_…`), **PyPI** (`pypi-…`), **SendGrid** (`SG.….…`) and **Twilio** API keys (`SK` and 32 hexadecimal digits).
- **Discord** bot tokens, checked by the bot id they start with, and **Telegram** bot tokens, also inside a Bot API address (`api.telegram.org/bot…/getMe`).
- **Private keys**: `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` blocks of every kind (RSA, EC, DSA, OpenSSH, PKCS #8, encrypted, PGP), also inside a JSON file such as a service account key, and also when the END line was not copied.
- **Database and queue addresses** with a password: `postgres://`, `postgresql://`, `mysql://`, `mariadb://`, `mongodb://`, `mongodb+srv://`, `redis://`, `rediss://`, `amqp://`, `amqps://`. An address without a password is kept.
- **`.env` lines** whose name says secret (`…_SECRET`, `…_TOKEN`, `…_API_KEY`, `…_PASSWORD`, `…_PASS`, `…_PASSPHRASE`, `SECRET_KEY`, `PRIVATE_KEY` and a few more), as in `.env` files, `export` lines and Docker Compose `environment` lists, when the value looks like a key or a password: no spaces, and a digit, a symbol between letters, or a long mix of capitals and small letters.
- **Two-factor seeds**: `otpauth://` and `otpauth-migration://` addresses, and authenticator exports in JSON (Aegis, 2FAS, LastPass Authenticator, andOTP, Bitwarden), where each seed sits next to an issuer, digits, a period or an algorithm. People paste such exports into the Authenticator extension's settings, so they pass through the clipboard.
- **JSON Web Tokens**, only when you turn them on. The JWT extension shows what is inside a token, and many people want to keep them, so they are kept by default.

## What it leaves alone

- Hashes, git commit ids, UUIDs, base64 data and images, and ordinary links, however long and random they look.
- Prefixes in prose, such as "tokens start with `ghp_`" or `sk-learn`, and anything too short or too long for its format.
- Placeholders, references and instructions: `API_KEY=your-api-key-here`, `TOKEN=changeme`, `PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}`, `SECRET_KEY=generate-a-long-random-string`, `mongodb+srv://<username>:<password>@…`, `sk-xxxxxxxx`.
- Default passwords from documentation and tutorials: `postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost`, `amqp://guest:guest@…`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=mysecretpassword`, a password that is its user's name, or one that says it is a password (`randompassword`, `dbpassword`).
- The words a program shows, even under a secret's name: `FORGOT_PASSWORD = "Forgot your password?"`, `HEADER_API_KEY = "X-Api-Key"`, `CSRF_TOKEN = "csrftoken"`.
- Code that names a secret without holding one: `token = get_token()`, `api_key=settings.API_KEY`, `password = os.environ["DB_PASSWORD"]`.
- Public keys, certificates, the sample keys in AWS's documentation, which end with `EXAMPLE`, and the sample two-factor seed in Google's description of otpauth links.
- Keys shown masked, as dashboards show them: `sk_live_••••a1b2`.

## Settings

- **Treat JSON Web Tokens as secrets**: off by default.

You can turn the rule off in Settings → Extensions, as any capture rule.

## Setup

Install Secret Guard from the Store in Settings → Extensions and allow its one permission. It works from the next copy on. Copies already in your history stay there: delete them by hand.

## Permissions and privacy

- **capture**, which you read as "Can see everything you copy": the rule has to see a copy before it is stored to keep a secret out. It is the only permission Secret Guard asks for.

Secret Guard sees your copies but has no way to send them anywhere. It has no network or program permission, and yabbistir runs capture rules without effects: a rule that tried to reach the network, run a program, read your history or show a notice would be refused. It writes nothing to disk or to its own storage, logs nothing, and returns only its decision: keep the copy, or do not store it. If a later version ever asked for another permission, it would wait until you approved it. The whole extension is one short file, [src/index.ts](src/index.ts), that you can read in a few minutes.

## Limits

- **It works silently.** A capture rule cannot show a notice, so nothing tells you a copy was left out of your history. If a copy is missing that you expected, it held something that looked like a secret.
- **Only known formats.** A password typed into a chat message, or a key with no known prefix and no label, is not recognized. Secret Guard would rather keep a copy than drop one by mistake.
- **Not every way to write a setting.** It reads `KEY=value` lines. YAML (`password: …`, and Docker Compose's `environment:` map, `KEY: value`), Java `.properties` keys with dots (`spring.datasource.password=…`) and Windows `set` lines are not recognized. A value is the rest of its line, without a ` #` comment, and a value with spaces never counts: a passphrase of words, or a line that runs a command after the value (`API_TOKEN=… npm start`).
- **Text and links only.** A screenshot of a key, or a key file copied in Finder, is not text, and no rule sees it.
- **Very long copies.** yabbistir decides whether a rule runs from the first 64 KB of a copy; a copy longer than that always goes to Secret Guard, which reads all of it. Copies over 256 KB meet no rule and are stored as they are.
- **The whole copy goes.** A long message or file with one secret in it is left out of your history whole; Secret Guard never stores a cleaned version, since yabbistir would also put that version on your clipboard.
readmes.dev.yabbistir.video-download:
# Download Video

Downloads a YouTube, Instagram or X link as an MP4 video or an M4A audio file with [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp). Copy a link, open the actions and choose *Download video*. Progress shows on the job card, and the finished file is handed back to yabbistir.

Video is requested as H.264 with AAC, which QuickTime plays on every Mac. When a site only has VP9 or AV1, or HE-AAC audio, the file is converted with ffmpeg.

## Permissions

- **network**, with `youtube.com`, `youtu.be`, `instagram.com`, `x.com` and `twitter.com`: the sites the extension works with, shown before you install it. The list holds the extension's own requests. yt-dlp is a separate program, so the list does not limit it: it reaches these sites and the servers they deliver media from (content networks such as `googlevideo.com`), as any download of such a link does.
- **exec**, limited to the tools below. The extension runs only `yt-dlp` and `ffmpeg` (and yt-dlp may call `deno`). It passes a fixed list of arguments and puts the link after `--`, so the link can never be read as an option.

## Tools to install

```sh
brew install yt-dlp ffmpeg deno
```

yt-dlp needs a JavaScript runtime to solve some sites' challenges (YouTube in particular), so `deno` is listed as a required tool too. If a download fails with a message about updating, run `brew upgrade yt-dlp`.

## Browser cookies (optional)

Some posts ask you to sign in. In the extension's settings, *Browser cookies* can be set to Safari, Chrome or Firefox. It is off by default and asks you to confirm when you turn it on.

Privacy: the extension reads no cookies itself. It only tells yt-dlp which browser to use (`--cookies-from-browser`), and the cookies go to yt-dlp and nowhere else. Safari needs Full Disk Access.

# Units & Currency

Recognizes a copy whose whole text is a number with a unit, or an amount of money, tags it, and converts it.

**Units.** Length (mm cm m km in ft yd mi), mass (mg g kg t oz lb st), temperature (°C °F K), volume (ml cl l, tsp tbsp fl oz cup pt qt gal), speed (km/h mph m/s kn), area (cm² m² ha km² in² ft² yd² acre mi²), data (B KB MB GB TB and KiB MiB GiB TiB) and time (ms s min h d wk, also `1h 30m`). The preview lists the sensible conversions: the other system first (metric to imperial and back), then the close neighbors. **Convert unit** pastes the main one; **Convert to all units** pastes the list, one per line.

**Currency.** `120 USD`, `$120`, `€50`, `₺1.250,50`, `50 EUR`, `100 TL`, `USD 120`, `1.250,50 ₺`. **Convert to TRY / EUR / USD / GBP** pastes the converted amount; **Convert to all currencies** pastes one line per currency. A text setting, *More currencies*, adds other ISO codes (for example `JPY, CHF`) to the list and to the preview.

## Example

Copy `72°F`: the tag *Unit* appears, the preview shows `22.22 °C` and `295.37 K`, and **Convert unit** pastes `22.22 °C`.
Copy `110 USD`, choose **Convert to EUR**: it pastes `€100.00` (at a rate of 1.10), and a notice says which day's rate was used.

## Permissions

- **network**, only to `www.ecb.europa.eu`. The rates come from the European Central Bank's daily reference rates (`https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-daily.xml`). The request carries nothing about the copied text, and only happens when you run a currency action, never while you copy or preview.

No tools, no other permissions.

## How rates work

- The ECB publishes the rates once on working days (about 16:00 Central European Time), for about thirty currencies against the euro. Other pairs are worked out through the euro. These are reference rates, not what a bank or card charges.
- The rates are kept on this Mac (`yab.storage`) with their date, and reused for six hours. After that the next currency action fetches them again.
- If the ECB can't be reached, the last saved rates are used and the notice says *Offline. Using the rate of <date>*. With no saved rates there is nothing to convert and you are told so.
- The preview never uses the network: it shows conversions from the saved rates and their date, or says that rates load the first time you convert.
- Source and terms: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates, free to reuse with the source named (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html). Unit factors are the exact definitions of the international yard and pound (1959), the US customary volumes, the knot (1852 m/h) and SI/IEC prefixes; nothing is copied from a third-party table.

## Notes and limits

- Only a **whole** text is recognized: `5 km` yes, `it is 5 km away` no.
- Numbers: `1,234.5`, `1.234,5`, `1 234,5`, `1'234.5` and `3,5` are all read. A lone separator followed by exactly three digits (`1,234`) is a thousands separator unless it is your language's decimal separator (so `1.234` is 1234 in Turkish and 1.234 in English).
- `KB`, `MB`… count 1000 bytes (as macOS does); `KiB`, `MiB`… count 1024. `Mb` and `Gb` (bits) are not recognized.
- `oz` is a mass; volume is `fl oz`. `t` is the metric tonne. `pt`, `qt`, `gal`, `cup`, `tbsp` and `tsp` are US measures. A bare `C` or `F` (capital) is a temperature; lowercase is not.
- `$` means US dollars and `¥` Japanese yen; use the code (`CAD`, `CNY`) for others. Only currencies the ECB publishes are supported.
- Temperatures below absolute zero, and numbers beyond 10^15, are not recognized.
- Months and years are not units (their length varies).

# Türkiye Pack

Understands the numbers you copy every day in Türkiye: IBANs, TC Kimlik and tax numbers, phone numbers and cargo tracking numbers. Everything is worked out on this Mac; nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose to track a package.

| You copy | Its chip | Its preview | ⇧ on it offers |
|---|---|---|---|
| An IBAN, of any country | IBAN | The IBAN in groups of four, the country, the check result and, for a Turkish IBAN, the bank's name and code | Format IBAN with spaces · Format IBAN without spaces |
| A TC Kimlik No | TCKN | Valid, and by which rule | |
| A tax number (VKN) | VKN | Valid, and by which rule | |
| A Turkish phone number | Phone | Mobile or landline, the province of a landline, the international form | Format with +90 · Format with a leading 0 · Format as E.164 |
| A cargo tracking number | | | Track with Yurtiçi Kargo · Aras Kargo · DHL eCommerce · UPS · DHL Express |

## Example

Copy `TR05 0006 4000 0000 0000 0012 34` (a made-up IBAN). It gets the *IBAN* chip, and its preview shows:

| | |
|---|---|
| IBAN | TR05 0006 4000 0000 0000 0012 34 |
| Country | Türkiye |
| Bank | Türkiye İş Bankası |
| Bank code | 00064 |
| Check | Valid · mod 97 |

Press ⇧ on it and *Format IBAN without spaces* shows `TR050006400000000000001234`, which ↵ pastes.

Copy `0532 000 00 01` and ⇧ offers `+90 532 000 00 01`, `0532 000 00 01` and `+905320000001`. Copy a Yurtiçi tracking number such as `100000000001`, pick *Track with Yurtiçi Kargo*, and Yurtiçi's tracking page opens in your browser with the number filled in.

## What it recognizes

The whole copied text must be the number (spaces and line breaks around it are ignored).

- **IBAN**: two letters for one of the 89 countries of the SWIFT IBAN Registry, the length that country uses, and check digits that pass ISO 7064 MOD 97-10. With or without spaces (non-breaking ones too), in upper or lower case, and after an `IBAN:` label. The bank is named from the five-digit code in positions 5 to 9 of a Turkish IBAN.
- **TC Kimlik No**: eleven digits, the first not 0, where the 10th digit is (7 × the sum of the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th digits − the sum of the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th) mod 10, and the 11th is the sum of the first ten mod 10.
- **VKN**: ten digits whose last is the check digit of the other nine. For the digit at position *i*: *p* = (digit + 10 − *i*) mod 10, *q* = *p* × 2^(10 − *i*) mod 9, or 9 when *p* is not 0 and *q* is; the check digit is 10 minus the sum of the *q*s, mod 10.
- **Phone number**: a mobile number (500–509, 530–559, and Turkcell's 516 and 561 series), a landline with a province's area code (and a subscriber number that does not start with 0 or 1), or an 850 or 800 number. Written with `+90`, `0090`, `90` or the trunk `0` in front, grouped with spaces or dashes, with the area code in brackets, or as one block: `+90 (532) 000 00 01`, `0 532 000 00 01`, `0532-000-00-01`, `05320000001`. A mobile number is also taken as ten bare digits, `5320000001`.
- **Tracking number**: ten digits (a DHL Express waybill), 12 to 22 digits (Yurtiçi, Aras, DHL eCommerce and others), a UPS `1Z` number, or a DHL `JJD` or `JD` piece number. Eleven digits never are, since in Türkiye those are a TC Kimlik No or a phone number with its 0, and neither are 90 or 0090 followed by ten digits that start like a Turkish number (with 2, 3, 4, 5 or 8). A tracking number gets no chip; the actions are offered on it.

## Tracking pages

Each carrier's own tracking page opens, with the number in its address. When yabbistir is in Turkish, the carriers' Turkish pages open.

| Carrier | Page |
|---|---|
| Yurtiçi Kargo | `https://www.yurticikargo.com/tr/online-servisler/gonderi-sorgula?code=<number>` (English: `/en/online-services/tracking?code=`). Takes 12 or 16 digits, as Yurtiçi's own page does; another number gets a short notice instead. |
| Aras Kargo | `https://kargotakip.araskargo.com.tr/mainpage.aspx?code=<number>` |
| DHL eCommerce (formerly MNG Kargo) | `https://kargotakip.dhlecommerce.com.tr/?takipNo=<number>`. The page asks you to type a short verification code before it shows the shipment. |
| UPS | `https://www.ups.com/track?loc=tr_TR&tracknum=<number>&requester=ST%2Ftrackdetails` (English: `loc=en_US`) |
| DHL Express | `https://www.dhl.com/tr-tr/home/tracking.html?tracking-id=<number>&submit=1` (English: `global-en`) |

**PTT Kargo and Sürat Kargo are not included**: their tracking pages take the number only together with a security check, and cannot be opened with the number in the address.

## Permissions

None. The extension reads only the item it is asked about. Opening a link in the browser (`yab.open`) needs no permission, and happens only when you pick a *Track with …* row: then the tracking number goes to that carrier's website, and nowhere else. TC Kimlik and tax numbers are never shown back in a preview or written to the log. A tax number is sent somewhere only if you pick a *Track with …* row on it, since ten digits are also a DHL Express waybill.

There are no programs to install and nothing to set up.

## Limits

- A check digit says a number is well formed, not that it was ever issued or whose it is. Only the check digits are tested, and the preview says so.
- About one in ten ten-digit numbers fits the single VKN check digit by chance, and about one in a hundred eleven-digit numbers fits both TC Kimlik rules, so an unrelated number of that length (a ten-digit Unix time, for example) can get the chip.
- Ten bare digits are taken as a phone number only when they start like a mobile number: `5320000001` is one, but a bare landline, 850 or 800 number such as `2122000001` needs its 0 or groups (`212 200 00 01`), since it is as likely some other number. About one bare mobile number in ten also fits the VKN check digit, and then gets both chips, since it could be either. 444 numbers, short numbers, extensions and numbers written with dots are not recognized.
- A ten-digit tax number or bare mobile number also looks like a DHL Express waybill, so *Track package* is offered on it too.
- Bank names come from the Central Bank's lists of 2026. A bank that has closed, or joined later, shows only its code.
- The IBAN check covers the length and the check digits, not the inner format of each country's account number. For a Turkish IBAN, the bank code and the reserve digit must also be digits, since the bank is named from them. Countries added to the registry after December 2024 are not recognized yet.
- Whether a carrier knows a tracking number is up to its own page.

## Sources

- **IBAN lengths**: [SWIFT IBAN Registry](https://www.swift.com/standards/data-standards/iban), Release 99 (December 2024), as summarized in [Wikipedia's IBAN article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bank_Account_Number#IBAN_formats_by_country). Only the country codes and lengths are used.
- **Bank codes and names**: the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (TCMB), [TCMB Ödeme Sistemleri Katılımcıları (2026)](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/9fa62a85-5b6d-46c5-9b01-eb461d43723d/TCMB+%C3%96deme+Sistemleri+Kat%C4%B1l%C4%B1mc%C4%B1lar%C4%B1+(072025).pdf?MOD=AJPERES) and [FAST Sistemi Katılımcı Listesi (2026)](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/954e041c-582d-4d1a-bd35-ff78e7c277b8/FAST+S%C4%B0STEM%C4%B0+KATILIMCILARI.pdf?MOD=AJPERES). Names are written without the company type (A.Ş.).
- **Area codes and mobile prefixes**: the +90 numbering plan of the Information and Communication Technologies Authority (BTK), as listed in [Telephone numbers in Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_numbers_in_Turkey).
- **TC Kimlik No rules**: [T.C. Kimlik Numarası](https://tr.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.C._Kimlik_Numaras%C4%B1) (Turkish Wikipedia).
- **VKN algorithm**: as implemented by [python-stdnum's `stdnum.tr.vkn`](https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/stdnum.tr.vkn), whose documented examples this one reproduces; no code was copied. The Revenue Administration's own check is its [VKN doğrulama](https://www.turkiye.gov.tr/gib-intvrg-vergi-kimlik-numarasi-dogrulama) service.
- **Tracking pages**: each carrier's tracking page (above), checked to take the number from its address: Yurtiçi's page script reads `code`, DHL eCommerce's page fills `takipNo` into its form, and Aras's page looks `code` up. The UPS and DHL addresses are the form their own sites use.

The embedded tables hold facts (country codes and lengths, bank codes and names, area codes and province names), not creative text, and no text or code from these sources is reproduced. The extension itself is MIT licensed.
